questions.stem: What is the SI unit of weight?
questions.explanation: Weight is a force and is measured in newtons (N). Mass is measured in kilograms (kg).

questions.stem: Which statement about mass is correct?

options.text: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and does not change with location
Mass is measured using a newton meter

questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in an object. It is a scalar quantity that remains the same regardless of location.

questions.stem: Calculate the weight of a 50 kg object on Earth (g = 10 N/kg).
questions.explanation: W = mg = 50 kg x 10 N/kg = 500 N.

questions.stem: An astronaut has a mass of 80 kg on Earth. What is their mass on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass does not change with location. The astronaut's mass remains 80 kg on the Moon, though their weight would be different due to weaker gravity.

questions.stem: The gravitational field strength on Mars is 3.7 N/kg. What is the weight of a 10 kg object on Mars?
questions.explanation: W = mg = 10 kg x 3.7 N/kg = 37 N.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure weight?
questions.explanation: Weight is measured using a newton meter (spring balance), which measures force. A balance is used to measure mass.

questions.stem: Why does weight change between Earth and the Moon but mass does not?

options.text: Because mass depends on gravity but weight does not
Because mass is measured in different units on the Moon
Because the Moon has no atmosphere
Because weight depends on gravitational field strength, which is different on the Moon

questions.explanation: Weight depends on gravitational field strength (W = mg). The Moon has a weaker gravitational field (1.6 N/kg vs 9.8 N/kg on Earth), so weight is less, but mass stays the same.
